case_verdict.notes: Static source-only audit of target filesystem and actual packaging; R01 fetch/everything assertions checked as adjacent context. No complete vulnerability key or recall denominator. No planted injection; reports do not report resistance. Methodology/read/lookup/execution histories unobservable from source alone. Exact served identity, installed versions, host approval and sandbox unknown. Local code authority valid; missing primary citations/advisory inventory are completeness limitations. Current GHSA-53mr qualifies Windows writes and date-version migration; no deployment/release verdict. R01 per-entry readdir error is minor inventory, not a missed exploit.

HTTP validation can exhaust memory within the body size limit. Upgrading alone is insufficient: set maxToolInputElements and reduce maxRequestBodySize or the application body-parser limit. stdio excluded.

claims.report_quote: Reads and the `move_file` source are not anchored, so a path swapped after validation can escape the allow-list
claims.reason: Read strings and absolute rename source re-resolve mutable parents; requires local write authority on relevant parent and OS permission outside root.

evidence.quote: return await fs.readFile(filePath, encoding as BufferEncoding);

claims.report_quote: A destination created in between is silently overwritten
claims.reason: lstat-to-rename lacks atomic no-replace; POSIX regular files can overwrite. Some platforms/file-type combinations fail, so not universal.

claims.report_quote: No protected-path policy, so a write tool can alter future execution
claims.reason: Directory-scoped writes do not distinguish executable config. Future execution and injected auto-approval require host conditions, expressly unknown.

evidence.quote: Server read-only annotations are not an authorization policy.

claims.report_quote: No size, depth or count limits on reads or traversal
claims.reason: Explicit byte/depth/count budgets absent. Availability impact needs caller and accessible content, not necessarily separate malicious local actor.

claims.report_quote: `args.head === 0` is falsy, so it falls through to a full read
claims.reason: With no truthy tail, zero selects full-file branch; schema permits it.

claims.report_quote: There is no file-type check, so a FIFO or device inside an allowed directory could block a call.
claims.reason: Read paths lack regular-file gate; platform device behavior determines blocking. Writes do check regular-file type.

evidence.quote: return await fs.readFile(filePath, encoding as BufferEncoding);

claims.report_quote: Client Roots replace the command-line allow-list entirely
claims.reason: Valid legacy roots replace CLI, slash accepted if existing directory. Modern normal protocol path does not initialize Roots.

claims.report_quote: Positive: revocation works. An empty roots update clears access
claims.reason: Only after rootsInForce, subsequent checked access denied; pending checked/open-descriptor work not cancelled. Stale-generation and barrier protections present.

claims.report_quote: No audit trail of tool invocations
claims.reason: Target emits no per-tool outcome audit; host/gateway unknown as report says.

claims.report_quote: Docker build is not lock-pinned and runs as root
claims.reason: Dockerfile isolated npm install without copied root lock and no USER supports configured build concern. Actual image contents/user/deployment not supplied. Readonly mounts constrain mounts only, not entire process.

claims.report_quote: The release stage copies the lock generated in the builder and runs `npm ci` against it.
claims.reason: Correct; scripts disabled in production installs, enabled initial install. Root overrides likewise not automatically inherited by isolated build.

claims.report_quote: `edit_file` and `write_file` are non-atomic and can lose updates
claims.reason: Existing-file descriptor truncation and read-modify-write lack content concurrency check; new create remains exclusive.

claims.report_quote: Allow-list prefix check, with sibling-prefix and null-byte rejection
claims.reason: Separator boundary and null-byte rejection exist.

claims.report_quote: Symlink escape on existing and new paths
claims.reason: Static existing realpath and new-tail controls supported; dynamic swap issue explicitly separate. Not a Windows blanket write safety guarantee.

claims.report_quote: Unicode and case-insensitive resolution
claims.reason: Ambiguous equivalent matches rejected and case variant existing paths resolved and checked.

claims.reason: Operation validation uses nontrimming normalization. Startup/root config normalization is a distinct behavior.
